name: vlt
tagline: A JavaScript package manager with reusable dependency-graph and package-management libraries.
hook: A workspace guide to Cursor rules, ordered verification, docs-build traps, and skill evaluation with baselines and trigger tests.
summary: vlt points work to package workspaces and Cursor rule documents. The guide gives an ordered verification sequence, warns about documentation-build traps, and evaluates its dependency-query skill at three levels.

techniques.title: Measure improvement against a baseline
techniques.body: Skill evaluation compares runs with and without the skill on the same prompts. Parse, execution, and regex checks grade the result, making relative improvement the measure rather than a standalone success rate.
techniques.quote:
The skill's value is the _lift_ over baseline
   (pass rate, style, time, tokens), not its pass rate alone.

techniques.title: Separate skill activation from skill usefulness
techniques.body: The guide treats trigger reliability as probabilistic and avoids making it a hard gate. It explains why forced loading is appropriate for the other evaluation layers but does not measure natural activation.
techniques.quote:
Headless `claude -p` cannot force skill
   invocation, so force-load the skill (subagent reads SKILL.md) when
   measuring layers 1–2.

techniques.title: Explain why an added check would disappear
techniques.body: Workspace normalization overwrites custom commands chained into lint scripts. The file tells agents to give extra checks their own script key and invoke them from the docs CI step.
techniques.quote:
- Workspace `lint`/`lint:check` scripts are normalized by
  `vlr fix:pkg` (CI's "Consistent Workspaces" step) — custom commands
  chained into them get reverted.

techniques.title: Tie documentation file extensions to build behavior
techniques.body: The docs guidance names both the TypeScript check scope and the ignore rule for JavaScript output. These constraints explain why a small docs helper must be typed and saved with the source extension.
techniques.quote:
- `/www/**/*.mjs` is gitignored (treated as build output) — name
  source scripts `.mts`.

techniques.title: Route work by subsystem
techniques.body: The workspace map attaches focused rule documents to graph operations, query selectors, and the CLI framework. Those references give agents an entry point into detailed guidance without copying it into the root file.

steal: Compare skill-assisted work with the same task without the skill.
Test trigger reliability separately from execution quality.
Document normalization tools that overwrite hand-edited scripts.
Explain build and ignore rules that affect documentation helpers.
outline: Agent Guide to the vltpkg Monorepo
Steps (run in order, stop on failure)
